target_customer: Makers and hobbyists first (consumer text-to-3D), moving toward mechanical engineers and hardware teams using Onshape and Fusion
problem: CAD tools are powerful but very hard to learn, so making a parametric part from an idea takes hours of expert work.
business_model: Freemium subscription (Standard and Pro tiers from about $5.99 and $17.99 per month); enterprise copilot not yet monetized as of Oct 2025

founders.name: Zach Dive
founders.background_notes: The product began as his master's thesis at Berkeley per the company thesis post.

founders.name: Avi
founders.role: Co-founder (surname and background not confirmed in opened sources)
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder in the YC launch post; the YC company page lists no background.

competitors.name: Zoo (Text-to-CAD)
competitors.what: Text-to-CAD generation producing B-Rep geometry, aimed at engineers

competitors.name: MecAgent
competitors.what: AI copilot for CAD, already available when TechCrunch covered Adam

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating parametric CAD code from prompts with LLMs was feasible for a tiny team in early 2025; reliable engineering-grade output for professional workflows is harder and was not yet claimed ready for enterprise per TechCrunch.

defensibility.rationale: Text-to-CAD wrappers around frontier models were easy to copy and several tools existed; the open-source CADAM release and a viral launch give distribution but not structural lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from opened sources. By late 2025 Adam was shipping copilots inside Onshape and Fusion rather than competing head on.

market_need_then: CAD is widely seen as complex and expensive to learn; TechCrunch reports tens of thousands of users and over 10 million social impressions from the text-to-3D app, showing consumer pull.

branding.domain_note: Uses adam.new, a .new domain; no purchase history found.

identity.logo: Simple wordmark; no description in opened sources

branding.brand_signature: Product also marketed as AdamCAD; CADAM open-source tool
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch cites over 10 million social impressions and Vercel founder Guillermo Rauch calling it the v0 of CAD.

brand_strength.rationale: Viral launch drove awareness, but the name is a common first name and also used as AdamCAD, which blurs it.

pivots.to: AI copilot for professional CAD workflows (Onshape, Fusion)
pivots.why: TechCrunch says the team targeted makers first because the technology was not yet ready for enterprise.

outcome_analysis: Adam went viral at its Winter 2025 launch with a free text-to-CAD tool, built a paying consumer base and raised a 4.1 million dollar seed from TQ Ventures in October 2025. It is moving from hobbyist 3D generation to professional CAD copilots, where incumbents and several text-to-CAD rivals compete. It remains active with no exit or distress reported.
notes: Seed amount confirmed by TechCrunch and several reposting outlets. One directory shows $500K, treated as an outlier. Zoo entry comes from a 2026 review, so it is not a founding-date source. Avi's surname and role (one search summary says CTO) not verified from an opened page.
